exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Hong Kong Director, Cathay two five one, inbound RIVER, descending to fow-er thousand feet, Information Juliet.
exchanges.meaning: Pilot's initial call to Hong Kong Director, inbound via RIVER, descending to 4,000 ft with ATIS Information Juliet.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay two five one, Hong Kong Director, cleared RNP Runway zero sev-en right approach, report LNAV and VNAV established.
exchanges.meaning: ATC clears the satellite-guided RNP approach for Runway 07R and requires a call when lateral and vertical guidance are captured.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Cleared RNP Runway zero sev-en right approach, report LNAV and VNAV established, Cathay two five one.
exchanges.meaning: Pilot reads back the RNP approach clearance and the LNAV/VNAV established reporting requirement verbatim.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Hong Kong Director, Cathay two five one, going around, loss of GPS RAIM integrity, climbing fow-er thousand feet heading zero seven three.
exchanges.meaning: Pilot initiates a go-around after losing GPS integrity past the FAF, advising ATC of the climb and heading.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay two five one, roger, fly missed approach, climb fow-er thousand feet, contact Hong Kong Radar wun two tree day-see-mal eight.
exchanges.meaning: Controller acknowledges the missed approach, confirms the climb, and hands the aircraft to Radar on 123.8.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Missed approach fow-er thousand feet, Radar wun two tree day-see-mal eight, Cathay two five one.
exchanges.meaning: Pilot reads back the missed approach climb and the Radar frequency transfer.

vocabulary.definition: Clearance authorizing a satellite-guided RNP approach; the aircraft flies published RF curved legs with on-board performance monitoring.
Mandatory pilot call when lateral (LNAV) and vertical (VNAV) guidance paths are captured on final approach.
Receiver Autonomous Integrity Monitoring failure — satellite geometry is insufficient for the approach; 5 satellites are needed to detect an error, 6 to isolate and exclude it (FDE).
Constant-radius curved turn flown on autopilot around terrain, enabling curved arrivals into mountainous valleys.
Failure annunciation (e.g. 'GPS PRIMARY LOST' / 'RAIM ALERT') requiring an immediate missed approach, especially past the FAF.
The defining RNP requirement: the aircraft system must guarantee containment (e.g. RNP 0.3 = within 0.3 NM 95% of the time) and alert pilots if total system error exceeds 0.6 NM.

quiz.question: What is the primary difference between Required Navigation Performance (RNP) and basic Area Navigation (RNAV)?
options: RNAV requires GPS; RNP requires ground VOR beacons.
RNP requires on-board performance monitoring and alerting (OBPMA), whereas RNAV does not.
RNP is only permitted for military aircraft.
RNAV cannot be used above 10,000 ft.
quiz.explanation: Under ICAO PBN specifications, the defining distinction of RNP is the requirement for on-board performance monitoring and alerting (OBPMA) to warn the pilot if navigational containment accuracy is degraded.

quiz.question: What action is required if a GPS RAIM warning occurs after passing the Final Approach Fix (FAF) on an RNP approach?
options: Execute an immediate Missed Approach and notify ATC of the loss of GPS integrity.
quiz.explanation: If GPS integrity monitoring fails past the FAF, the approach is no longer approved for obstacle clearance. The flight crew must immediately execute a missed approach and advise ATC.

sections.heading: Section 2: Core Learning Content & Vocabulary Table
sections.body:
| Phrase / Command | ICAO Standard Definition | Phonetic Guide | Operational Example |
|---|---|
| Cleared RNP Runway [num] | Clearance authorizing satellite-guided RNP approach. | kleerd ar-en-pee... | "Cleared RNP Runway 07R approach." |
| Report LNAV/VNAV established | Mandatory call when lateral & vertical paths are captured. | re-PORT el-nav vee-nav... | Confirms guidance on final approach. |
| RAIM warning / alert | Receiver Autonomous Integrity Monitoring failure. | RAY-im WORN-ing | Satellite geometry insufficient for approach. |
| Radius-to-Fix (RF) leg | Constant-radius curved turn flown on autopilot around terrain. | RAY-dee-us to fix leg | Enables curved arrival into mountainous valleys. |
| Loss of GPS integrity | Failure annunciation requiring immediate missed approach. | loss of G-P-S in-TEG-ri-tee | "Going around, loss of GPS integrity." |

sections.heading: Section 8: Spaced Repetition Review Drill
sections.body:
- Day 32 Review (+1d): ILS glide path must always be intercepted from below to prevent locking onto false 6° or 9° ground reflection lobes.
- Day 31 Review (+2d): Localizer full-scale deflection is only ±2.5°. Report "Established on localizer" prior to Tower transfer.

sections.heading: Section 9: Fun Aviation Fact — Mountain Approaches of Queenstown & Paro
sections.body: Before RNP, airports surrounded by towering mountains like Paro, Bhutan or Queenstown, New Zealand could only operate in severe visual weather because straight-line radio signals bounce off rock walls. With RNP "Radius-to-Fix" (RF) curved legs, modern airliners fly blind through narrow winding river canyons on autopilot, banking around mountain ridges with sub-meter accuracy right down to the runway threshold!
